posts.title: Customer asked the price and stopped replying? Here's why, and what to send
posts.excerpt: Buyers rarely say no. They go quiet for a reason: the price, delivery, trust, fit or paying. How to tell which one it is, and the one move that fits each.

posts.title: The most expensive message in your inbox is the one you didn't answer

posts.excerpt: Most CRMs are built for sales departments with pipelines and quotas. Most chat stores have a sheet and a founder. When to stay, when to move.

news.title: Integrations
news.excerpt: Instagram, WhatsApp, your store and your payment link now feed one place. Every chat arrives with its product, stock and payment details attached, so you answer without switching tabs.

news.title: WhatsApp opens coexistence to more markets
news.excerpt: More businesses can now run the WhatsApp Business app and the Cloud API on the same number. Sellers keep replying from their phone while tools read and route the same chats. It removes the old choice between replying from your phone and using a tool.
news.take: This is the setup we built around. If you held off on tools to keep your phone, you no longer have to.

news.title: Recovery, rebuilt as one list
news.excerpt: Quiet buyers now sit in one list, banded Act now, Still warm and Fading, and sorted by who's worth chasing. Open any row for the full lead file: their last words, why they stalled, how long you have, and the reply to send.

news.title: Instagram tightens the 7-day messaging window for businesses
news.excerpt: Business accounts can reply freely for seven days after a buyer's last message. After that, only narrow tagged replies are allowed, and automated follow-ups get stricter review. Quiet buyers past a week now need a comment or story reply to reopen the chat.
news.take: Day 3 to day 6 is now the real recovery window on Instagram. Chase inside it.

news.title: Insights
news.excerpt: See where buying chats stopped this week and why: slow replies, no payment link, links left unpaid, silence after the price. Every count opens the chats behind it.

news.title: Chat is now the first touchpoint for most small D2C orders
news.excerpt: Surveys of small direct-to-consumer brands keep finding the same thing: a growing share of first orders start in a DM, not on the product page. Price, size and delivery questions dominate, and most go unanswered for hours.
news.take: The store page is where they pay. The chat is where they decide.

news.title: Specs proposed from chats
news.excerpt: When several buyers ask the same question about a product, the answer arrives as a spec to accept. One tap fills it in and your drafts start quoting it. Nothing in your store changes without you.

news.title: Faster ranking on busy mornings
news.excerpt: Priority Today now builds in under a minute for stores with more than 500 open chats. Your lineup is ready before you open the app, even after a launch weekend.

news.title: Pay-in-chat links become the default checkout for social sellers
news.excerpt: Payment providers are shipping lighter links built for DMs: one tap, saved details, and status that reports back to the seller. Abandonment drops when the link arrives right after the buyer says yes, not an hour later.
news.take: Send the link the moment they confirm a size. Speed beats a discount here.

news.title: Early access opens in waves
news.excerpt: We're adding sellers in waves so every store gets a hands-on setup call. The waitlist stays open, and the free audit is still the fastest way in.

news.title: Per-message pricing replaces conversation pricing
news.excerpt: Template messages are now billed per message instead of per 24-hour conversation, and replies inside the service window stay free. Businesses that answer fast pay less; mass follow-ups cost more.
news.take: Good news for sellers who reply fast. Answer inside the window.

news.title: Snooze for the right day
news.excerpt: Snooze a quiet buyer until the day a promo starts or a restock lands. They come back to your list on that day, not before, so you nudge with a real reason to reply.

news.title: Bots answer first, humans still close
news.excerpt: Brands using chatbots report faster first replies but flat conversion on high-intent chats. The pattern across stores: bots handle FAQs well, and buyers ready to pay still wait for a person.
news.take: Let the bot sort. Keep the close human.

news.title: Story replies stop counting as leads
news.excerpt: Emoji-only story reactions are now tucked out of the way instead of filling your inbox, so the buyers asking about products stay in front and your counts stop inflating on post days.
